analysis: This batch contains documentation only: the new changelog.d/ssd-eviction-selection.md (head lines 1-13) and docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (head line 3 date bump and head lines 531-550). Both describe a change to SSD LRU eviction victim selection in SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest. The new flow makes one linear SSDBlockIndex.oldest probe. Only if that victim is busy or undeletable does it fall back to a heap-based oldestFirstSnapshot. A pass ends early when the store is closed. Relevant threat: T-041 (SSD tier at-rest exposure bounded by TTL and the LRU disk budget; mitigation (b)). The docs say file leases, epoch validation and the removal lock still govern retirement. External-loss reconciliation still returns control to the disk budget, and a closed store, which never reopens, frees nothing. None of these claims changes the HMAC naming, AAD, TTL, KEK purge, salt scoping or gating that T-041 depends on. The source file SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift and SSDBlockIndex are not in this batch, so the documented behavior is unverified here. Integration should check: (1) the snapshot bounds attempts so a busy or undeletable set cannot cause unbounded loops (availability). (2) Ending the pass early on a closed store does not stop eviction in other stores or let the disk budget be exceeded indefinitely, which would weaken the T-041 LRU budget. (3) A snapshot taken before the first attempt cannot delete a file that was replaced or touched concurrently while it is leased or adopted, so leases are still honored. (4) The excluded first tag is handled correctly. No regression is evident from the docs alone; this is a coverage limit, not proof of safety.
